column1: # seance -- the promotion ladder's truth table (TESTING.md §5).
# Every rung crossed with every outcome the infrastructure can produce, and
# every crossing with ONE expected disposition. The driver is
# tests/tier4/t_ladder.sh; nothing here is interpreted anywhere else.
#   id       a name for the row, used in the assertion text
#   world    space-separated settings the driver builds a world from:
#              nodes=<2|3|4>      cluster size in the configuration
#              reach=<n>          how many living peers answer ssh
#              dead=<no|ping|ssh> whether the "dead" node answers, and how
#                                   missing    a driver name nothing provides
#                                   targetless a driver with no fence_target
#                                 default), this node SECOND behind an heir
#                                 that is somewhere else, or no heir at all
#              claim=<-|charlie>  a living peer that already claims the guest
#              guest=<web01|db01> web01 is a jail, db01 a bhyve VM
#                                 what the guest's own configuration says about
#                                 where its data lives, and whether that
#                                 configuration travels inside its own replica
#                                 what the platform reports about the guest's
#                                 data path once it has been registered
#              auto=<0|1>         drive the ladder as devd would (--auto)
#              carp=<state>       what adapter_carp_state says AFTER the
#                                 debounce: MASTER is a death, anything else
#              vhid=<yes|no>      whether the dead node has a vhid at all
#              override=<node>    a per-guest heir override naming that node,
#                                 so that the guest's actor is not this node
#   force    the --force value, or '-' for no --force at all; '' (empty) is
#            not expressible here, so 'all' means a bare --force
#   disp     expected PROMOTE_DISPOSITION, or '-' for none set
#   evidence expected PROMOTE_EVIDENCE, with %OP% standing for the operator
#   stopped  expected PROMOTE_STOPPED_RUNG, or '-' for "the ladder finished"
#   exit     expected exit status of promote_run
# --- rung 3: a host that answers is never fenced ----------------------------
# --- rung 4: the fence driver's exit-code contract --------------------------
# --- configurations that pass --check and are hostile anyway (battery a) ----
# The succession is the fleet's, not this node's opinion of it: a node that is
# second in the queue acts only when the first cannot, and a node in no queue
# --- rung 2: quorum, and the even-N doctrine --------------------------------
# --- rung 5: lineage, claims and kernel homogeneity -------------------------
# --- --force skips EXACTLY the rungs it names -------------------------------
# --- the promotion point is the newest instant the WHOLE tree exists at (D-85)
# --- a jail's configuration, which does not travel with its data (D-82) -----
# --- where a replica is mounted is READ, never derived (D-178, D-181) -------
# The path comes out of the guest's own rc.conf, before anything is mounted,
# from whichever replica carries that file. What the rows are about:
#   jailshape  the first real fleet -- a bhyve guest whose data lives at the
#              jail-shaped path, which the type's creation convention would
#   travels    the configuration inside the guest's own replica, which is
#              where a VM on CBSD keeps it (sudoexec/bcreate:599)
#   relative   a configuration naming a path a replica cannot be mounted at:
#              a REFUSAL, and never a quiet fall back to the convention
#   disagree   the platform, asked after the registration, reports the guest's
#              data somewhere other than where the replica was mounted
# --- the notify contract: never changes a rung's disposition ----------------
# --- the automatic path: devd is the trigger and no human is anywhere -------
# and the rungs that stop a manual promotion stop an automatic one identically
# --- a per-guest override the automatic path cannot act on (D-129, D-130) ----
# --- what the automatic path tells a human, and when (D-122) -----------------
